golden_comments.comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. The old code included a `booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }` filter when deleting workflow reminders, ensuring only reminders belonging to the current user's bookings were deleted. The new code removes this authorization check entirely. An attacker who can trigger a workflow update (e.g., by modifying event type associations) could cause reminders belonging to other users' bookings to be cancelled or deleted without authorization.

[High] Missing await on async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls in workflow deletion

Multiple places in workflows.tsx (lines 211, 375, 517, 572) call async delete functions without await inside forEach loops. The old code had await Promise.all(deleteReminderPromise) which ensured database operations completed. Now the async operations are fire-and-forget.

The old code deleted workflow reminder records from the database after cancelling scheduled jobs. The new code only calls the delete functions (which mark reminders as cancelled) but doesn't delete the DB records. The batch cancellation in scheduleEmailReminders.ts provides partial mitigation but introduces a timing window where cancelled reminders could still be processed.

[Medium] Removed batch DB deletion, replaced with individual deletes inside functions

Previously, all workflow reminder deletions were batched into a single `Promise.all` with `deleteMany` queries. Now, each reminder's deletion is handled individually inside `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` or `deleteScheduledSMSReminder`, which each make a separate DB call. For a booking with 5 reminders, this changes from 1 batch query to 5 individual queries. This pattern is repeated across multiple files (handleCancelBooking.ts, bookings.tsx, workflows.tsx).

[High] Missing await on async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls

The forEach callback calls async functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder without await. These functions perform API calls and database operations. Without await, the cancellation may not complete before the function returns, and errors are silently swallowed. The old code had the same issue but it's now more critical because the functions do more work (DB operations).

The `for` loop on line 55 iterates over `remindersToCancel` and makes individual `await client.request(...)` calls sequentially. This means each API call waits for the previous one to complete. If there are many cancelled reminders (e.g., 100+), this could take 10+ seconds per minute, potentially causing the cron job to overlap with itself. Should use `Promise.all` to send cancellation requests concurrently.

[Medium] New query with loop adds O(n) DB and API operations to cron job

A new `findMany` query fetches all cancelled reminders in the next hour, then iterates over them with individual API calls and individual DB deletes. Previously, cancelled reminders were handled inline during booking cancellation. This adds a new O(n) workload to a cron job that runs every minute. The forEach callback calls async functions without await. The try/catch only catches synchronous errors, not promise rejections. The async operations are fire-and-forget, so workflow reminders from the original booking may not be properly cancelled during rescheduling.

deleteScheduledSMSReminder always deletes the reminder from the database after cancelling via Twilio. However, deleteScheduledEmailReminder (without immediateDelete=true) only marks the reminder as cancelled (cancelled: true) without deleting it. [High] Missing await on async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls

https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/8.pr_title: Advanced date override handling and timezone compatibility improvements

golden_comments.comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime

Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

review_comments.body:
[High] Date override bypasses busy check allowing double-booking

The `checkIfIsAvailable` function now returns `true` immediately when a date override exists for the slot's date, without checking if the user is busy. This means any time slot on a day with a date override will be considered available, even if the user has existing bookings that overlap with that slot. The busy check at the end of the function is completely bypassed when `dateOverrideExist` is true.

[High] Expensive dateOverrides iteration inside checkIfIsAvailable called per slot

The `checkIfIsAvailable` function now iterates over the entire `dateOverrides` array (potentially 365+ items per user) for every slot check. Inside the `.find()` callback, multiple `dayjs` operations are performed including `dayjs.tz()`, `.utcOffset()`, `.format()`, `.isBefore()`, `.isSame()`, `.isAfter()`. This function is called for every slot for every user in the availability check. For a typical scenario with 96 slots, 10 users, and 365 date overrides per user, this results in ~350,000 expensive dayjs operations per request. The `workingHours.find()` adds additional overhead per slot.

[High] Dayjs object comparison using === instead of .isSame()

Line 108 compares two Dayjs objects using === which performs reference comparison, not value comparison. This will always be false even if the dates are equal, causing the condition to never trigger. Should use dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, 'minutes')).

[High] Inverted date override slot containment check

Lines 110-116 return true (causing the slot to be rejected) when the slot is OUTSIDE the override range. This is inverted logic - if the slot is outside the override, the code should continue checking other overrides, not immediately reject. The find() callback should return true only when the slot IS within the override range (meaning this override applies and the slot should be accepted).

[High] Working hours end time calculation uses start time instead of end time

Line 139 calculates `end` as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` which is identical to `start`. This means the working hours check never verifies if the slot extends beyond the working hour end time. The correct calculation should use `slotEndTime` instead of `slotStartTime`.

[High] Missing timeZone property on schedule object

Line 492 passes `organizerTimeZone: schedule.timeZone` to checkIfIsAvailable, but `schedule` is the schedule object (TimeRange[][]) which does not have a `timeZone` property. The timeZone is on the user availability object, not on the schedule. This will pass undefined as organizerTimeZone, causing the date override logic to use utcOffset = 0.

[Medium] Potential undefined timeZone on userSchedule

Line 517 passes `organizerTimeZone: userSchedule?.timeZone` but `userSchedule` is the result of `userAvailability.find()` which returns an availability object. The availability object has a `timeZone` property, but if no matching user is found, `userSchedule` is undefined and `?.timeZone` will be undefined. This could happen if a slot has a userId that doesn't match any user in userAvailability.

[Medium] Increased dayjs operations in getSlots overrides processing

The `activeOverrides.flatMap` now creates 4 `dayjs` instances per override (previously 0) with timezone conversions and arithmetic. For 365 overrides, this adds ~1460 dayjs operations per call to `getSlots`.

https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/1.pr_title: OAuth credential sync and app integration enhancements

golden_comments.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
Invalid Zod schema syntax. Computed property keys like [z.string().toString()] are not valid in Zod object schemas and will cause runtime errors.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

review_comments.body:
[High] Weakened token validation when credential sharing is enabled

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, parseRefreshTokenResponse uses a minimumTokenResponseSchema that only validates access_token is a string and there's at least one numeric property. This bypasses app-specific validation schemas that may check for required fields like refresh_token, expiry_date, or other provider-specific fields. Additionally, if refresh_token is missing from the response, it's set to the literal string 'refresh_token', which is invalid and will cause authentication failures.

[High] Invalid Zod schema for minimum token response

The line `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` evaluates to a computed property key `"[object Object]"` instead of creating a catch-all for string keys with number values. This means the schema will only match objects that have a property literally named `[object Object]` with a number value, which will never match real API responses. The intended behavior was likely to allow any string key with a number value, which should use `z.record(z.string(), z.number())` or similar.

[Medium] No validation of response from credential sync endpoint

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, refreshOAuthTokens fetches tokens from the sync endpoint and returns the raw response without any validation of the response structure, content, or format. This means any data returned by the sync endpoint will be treated as valid tokens and stored in the credentials table.

[Medium] External HTTP call on every token refresh when credential sharing is enabled

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is configured, every OAuth token refresh now makes an HTTP POST to an external endpoint before proceeding. This adds network latency to every token refresh operation across all OAuth-based app integrations (Google Calendar, Office365, HubSpot, Lark, Webex, Zoho Bigin). Token refreshes happen periodically (~hourly per user) and are on the critical path for calendar operations when tokens expire.

[High] Return type mismatch when sync endpoint is used

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response object. However, all callers expect specific data shapes: Google expects `{data: {access_token, expiry_date}}`, Hubspot expects a HubspotToken object, Lark expects a Response with specific methods, etc. This will cause runtime errors (e.g., `res?.data` will be undefined on a Response object) when the sync endpoint is configured.

[High] New webhook endpoint for credential management without user authorization

This new API endpoint allows creating or updating credentials for any user by providing a userId, appSlug, and encrypted keys. While it checks for a webhook secret header, there is no authorization check to verify that the caller has permission to manage credentials for the specified user. If the webhook secret is compromised, an attacker can create or update credentials for any user in the system.

[Medium] New refresh token logic in Salesforce CalendarService uses weakened validation

The Salesforce CalendarService now has a new refresh token flow that makes a direct HTTP request to Salesforce and uses parseRefreshTokenResponse to validate the response. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, this uses the weakened minimumTokenResponseSchema instead of the app-specific salesforceTokenSchema, potentially allowing invalid token data to be stored.

[High] Blocking HTTP call in CalendarService constructor

The constructor of SalesforceCalendarService now makes a synchronous HTTP POST to Salesforce's OAuth token endpoint and a Prisma DB update before returning the connection object. This means every instantiation of the service (which happens for every calendar operation: list events, create event, update event, delete event) will incur a ~200-500ms network round-trip to Salesforce. Previously the constructor was synchronous and only set up the connection object. This is a severe regression because it adds blocking I/O to a frequently-called constructor path.

[High] Async operations in non-async constructor

The SalesforceCalendarService constructor performs async operations (fetch, response.json, parseRefreshTokenResponse, prisma.credential.update) but the constructor is not async. These operations will start but not be awaited, causing the constructor to return before the credential is updated. The connection is returned immediately, and the credential update may happen later or not at all, leading to stale credentials being used.

[High] Wrong variable passed to refreshOAuthTokens

The call to refreshOAuthTokens passes `credentialId` as the third argument (userId), but `credentialId` is not defined in this scope. The variable should be `credential.userId` or similar. This causes the sync endpoint to receive `undefined` as the user ID, breaking credential sync functionality.

golden_comments.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

review_comments.body:
[High] DeleteMany query uses OR instead of AND, potentially deleting unintended reminders

The deleteMany query was changed from deleting only SMS reminders with past scheduled dates to deleting reminders where (method=SMS AND scheduledDate <= now) OR (retryCount > 1). This means any reminder with retryCount > 1 will be deleted regardless of method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, etc.) or scheduled date (could be in the future). This could cause legitimate reminders to be deleted prematurely if their retryCount exceeds 1.

[Medium] Retry count incremented on successful SMS scheduling

When SMS scheduling succeeds (scheduledSMS.sid exists), the code increments retryCount. This is unusual because retry counts should typically only be incremented on failures. If the scheduling logic runs multiple times for the same reminder (e.g., due to race conditions or multiple API calls), retryCount would increase even on success, potentially causing the reminder to be deleted by the cleanup query once retryCount exceeds 1.

https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/1.pr_title: Add guest management functionality to existing bookings

golden_comments.comment: Case sensitivity bypass in email blacklist

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
This calls the email sender with the original guests, so existing attendees included in the input will be treated as new when sending notifications, leading to incorrect emails.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

review_comments.body:
[Medium] Blacklist bypass via case sensitivity

The blacklist check compares guest emails against lowercased blacklist entries, but does not lowercase the guest email before comparison. An attacker can bypass the blacklist by using a case-variant of a blacklisted email address.

[Medium] No validation that added guests are actual users

The handler accepts any valid email address without verifying that the person exists in the system. An attacker who is an attendee can add arbitrary email addresses as guests, causing unwanted calendar invitations and emails to be sent to non-users.

[High] Non-existent property `userPrimaryEmail` on booking object

The code accesses `booking?.userPrimaryEmail` but this property does not exist on the Prisma Booking type. The booking query does not include a `userPrimaryEmail` field, and it's not a standard field in the database schema. This will result in `undefined` being used as the organizer email in the CalendarEvent, potentially causing email delivery failures or incorrect sender information.

[Medium] Potential undefined teamId passed to permission functions

The code passes `booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0` to `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner`. If `booking.eventType` is null (which is possible for some booking types), `teamId` will be undefined and fall back to 0. Passing 0 as teamId to these functions may cause unexpected behavior or incorrect permission checks, as team ID 0 likely doesn't exist.

[Medium] Concurrent email sending without rate limiting or queue

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function sends all emails concurrently using `Promise.all`. For each guest addition, it sends: 1 email to the organizer, N emails to team members (where N = team size), and M emails to attendees (where M = number of attendees). This means 1 + N + M emails are sent simultaneously. For large teams (e.g., 100+ members) or bookings with many attendees (e.g., 50+), this could overwhelm the email service provider, trigger rate limiting, or cause timeouts. The emails are sent as part of a synchronous user request, so the user waits for all emails to be sent before getting a response.

[High] Wrong email template sent to new guests

In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the condition `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` to new guests. This is incorrect - new guests should receive `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` (notification they were added to an event), not `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (which is for initial booking confirmation). Additionally, existing attendees receive `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` which is also wrong - they should receive a notification that new guests were added, but the template name suggests it's designed for the new guests themselves.

[High] XSS via raw_html cook_method bypasses HTML sanitization

The new `cook_method` option allows posts to be rendered as raw HTML without going through the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. When `cook_method` is set to `:raw_html`, the `cook` method returns the raw content directly. This is used by `TopicEmbed.import` for RSS feed imports and remote URL imports. Any malicious HTML or JavaScript in the imported content will be rendered as-is in the post view and embed views.

[High] Command injection via open() in import_remote

The `import_remote` method uses Ruby's `open()` function to fetch content from a URL. In Ruby, `open()` can execute shell commands if the URL starts with a pipe character (`|`). The URL comes from user input via `EmbedController#best` and is only validated against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` in `TopicRetriever`. If the host validation passes or is not configured, an attacker can provide a URL like `| command` to execute arbitrary system commands.

[Medium] SSRF via embed_url parameter with insufficient host validation

The `EmbedController#best` action accepts an `embed_url` parameter from unauthenticated users and passes it to `TopicRetriever` which fetches the URL. The host validation only checks against a single configured `embeddable_host`. If this setting is empty or matches a common host, an attacker can make the server fetch arbitrary URLs, including internal services (e.g., http://169.254.169.254/ for cloud metadata, http://localhost:9200/ for Elasticsearch).

[Medium] Missing authentication on embed endpoints allows unauthenticated job triggering

The `EmbedController` skips `check_xhr` and `preload_json` filters and has no authentication requirement. Any unauthenticated user can call the `best` action with an `embed_url` parameter, which enqueues a `retrieve_topic` job. This can be used to trigger SSRF attacks or exhaust server resources by flooding the job queue.

[Medium] SSRF via feed_polling_url site setting

The `Jobs::PollFeed` scheduled job uses `open()` on `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url` without validating the URL scheme or host. While this is a site setting (requires admin access), if an attacker gains admin access or if there's a configuration vulnerability, they can point this to internal services or use the `|` pipe for command injection.

[Medium] Unbounded feed item processing without batching

The PollFeed job iterates over all items in an RSS/ATOM feed without any pagination, batching, or limit. For each item, it performs at least one database query (TopicEmbed.where) and potentially creates/updates topics and posts. With a feed containing hundreds or thousands of items, this single job execution will perform an equivalent number of sequential database operations, potentially causing long-running jobs, database contention, and timeout issues.

[Medium] Full feed poll triggered for single missing embed

When a single embed URL is not found in the database, TopicRetriever.perform_retrieve calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) which processes the ENTIRE RSS feed. This means a single user request for an embed can trigger processing of hundreds of feed items, even though only one is needed. This is extremely wasteful and can cause significant latency for the requesting user.

The migration adds `cook_method` column with `default: 1`. However, `Post.cook_methods` is defined as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` where `:regular = 0` and `:raw_html = 1`. This means ALL existing posts will have `cook_method = 1` (raw_html) after migration. The `cook` method in `post.rb` now returns `raw` without processing when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. This causes every existing post to display unprocessed raw HTML instead of cooked content, breaking the entire forum's post rendering.
